bottleneck: ALS kills motor neurons in 2-5 years, yet its cause is unknown in 90% of cases: dozens of implicated genes, plus protein aggregation, excitotoxicity, and glial dysfunction, with no unifying mechanism. Antisense drugs for SOD1-ALS help a genetic minority; sporadic ALS has no targeted therapy. Trial failures are the norm because the disease being treated is not understood, and the rapid course leaves little room for trial-and-error or slow dose-finding.
current_state: Riluzole and edaravone offer months of benefit. Research fragments across competing mechanisms without a validated causal model, and combination trials are only beginning.
title: ALS mechanism unknown in most cases
why_it_blocks: A rapidly fatal disease with no causal model cannot be rationally drugged. ALS exemplifies the cost of treating symptoms of an unknown process — years of trials, months of benefit.
